speaker: Rocco
intro: Ba-dum-TSS! Rocco Rimshot, drummer of The Decibelles. Thirty years behind the kit, not one earplug!
Thirty years of cymbals and no earplugs? My feathers just curled.
My bandmates' jokes have lost their punchlines. In noisy pubs I laugh at the wrong bits.
And my ears ring like a cymbal that never stops.
Ringing ears and lost punchlines. Let's investigate! Questions first.

always_clues.text: 30 years of loud drumming, no earplugs

options: Is it worse in quiet, or in noise?
Quiet chat's fine. Noisy pub, I laugh at the wrong bits.
Fine in quiet, lost in noise
noise_trouble
Hearing but not understanding: the high pitches carry the consonants.
What's your favourite drum?
The cowbell. Criminally underrated.
Which ear is worse?
About the same. Maybe the left: that's my hi-hat side.
Both ears, about the same
both_ears
Any ear pain, drainage, dizziness, or sudden change?
No pain, no gunk, no spinning. It crept up over the years.
No pain, drainage, dizziness or sudden change
no_red_flags
When was your last loud gig?
Saturday. Nothing loud since. My neighbours are thrilled.
No loud sound for 4 days
rested
Good. Right after loud sound, hearing can dip for a day or two.
Can you do a drum solo for me?
*drums on the desk* Ba-da-ba-da-ba-da TSSSS! ...What was the question?

joke_line: Groovy, but not a clue. Ask about his hearing!

red_flags.ask_line: Always check the red flags: pain, drainage, dizziness, sudden or fluctuating change, one ear only.
red_flags.answer: None of those. It crept up, year after year, gig after gig.
red_flags.clue: No pain, drainage, dizziness or sudden change
red_flags.card: Pain, drainage, dizziness, sudden change: NONE.

after_history: Crept up slowly, no red flags so far. Let's look inside!

otoscopy.caption: Rocco's RIGHT ear: a roomy canal, shiny eardrum.
lines: Roomy canals, healthy eardrums. No drumsticks stuck in there either.
You'd be surprised what ends up in a drummer's ear.

tymp.clue: Tymp: type A both ears (no fluid, no blockage)
after: Type A both sides: no fluid, no blockage. The bone test will tell us if it's deeper.

instructions: Tell him: press for every beep, even faint ones. Not for the cymbal in his head!
Beeps yes, ringing no. Got it, boss.

audiometry.intro: Right ear's yours, up to 8k. Watch what happens between 4k and 8k!
Left ear at Hoot speed. Same pattern?
Bone check at Hoot speed: middle ear or inner ear?
before: Now the bone buzzer, on his right: is it the middle ear, or deeper?

after_audiometry: Unmasked bone matches both ears' air: no gap on either side.

reveal.title: NOISE NOTCH
ask: Here's Rocco's chart, trainee. What shape do you see?
lines: Dip at 4k, back up at 8k: a noise notch. It points to years of loud sound.
So my drums wrote their name in my ears?
Pretty much. The damage so far is permanent. More damage is preventable.

evidence.prompt: What shape is Rocco's hearing loss?
options: A notch: a dip at 4k that recovers at 8k.
A ski slope: worse and worse up to 8k.
Rising: worse in the low pitches.
wrong: Look at 8k: it climbs back up. A ski slope keeps going down.
His low pitches are fine. Look at the right side of the chart.
evidence.right: Noise notches usually sit between 3k and 6k, deepest near 4k.

lines.fit: No red flags, and he misses words in noisy pubs: hearing aids help. Earplugs every gig!
lines.refer: Careful is good! But no red flags: ears match, no pain, no spins, nothing sudden.
lines.today: Nothing sudden: it crept up over thirty years of drumming. Not an emergency.

clue_pick.prompt: Present the evidence: why is it safe to fit Rocco today?
clue_pick.wrong_line: True, but it doesn't prove he's safe to fit. Look for the red-flag check!

wrong_lines.noise_years: That's why he has a loss, not why it's safe to fit. Find the red-flag check!
wrong_lines.noise_trouble: That's why he WANTS hearing aids. What shows it's safe to fit them?
wrong_lines.notch: That's the pattern, not the safety check. Find the red-flag check!
wrong_lines.ear_clear: True, the exam looks clean. Which clue clears pain, dizziness and sudden change?
wrong_lines.tymp_a: True, the exam looks clean. Which clue clears pain, dizziness and sudden change?
wrong_lines.snhl: True, the exam looks clean. Which clue clears pain, dizziness and sudden change?

clue_pick.right_line: Exactly! Nothing on the red-flag list, and ears that match: fitting is the right call.

payoff: Hearing aids tuned for the high pitches. They often make the ringing less noticeable, too.
Whoa. I can hear the hi-hat AND my bandmates' terrible jokes!
Now protect what's left: earplugs at every gig AND every rehearsal.

options: Cotton wool
Cotton wool? It barely blocks a thing, and it just fell in the snare.
Foam earplugs
Foam works, but it muffles the highs. A drummer wants it even.
Musicians' earplugs
Flat, even quieting: the cymbals still sound like cymbals. Rock on, safely!

payoff: On stage: hearing aids out, earplugs in. And a hearing check every year.

headlines.S: DRUMMER'S NOTCH NAILED; OWL PRESCRIBES EARPLUGS
headlines.A: ROCCO HEARS HI-HAT AGAIN; PUB DEMANDS QUIETER SOLOS
headlines.B: NOTCH FOUND, DRUMMER FITTED, CYMBALS ON NOTICE
headlines.C: SOME BEEPS DROPPED THE BEAT, CONFIRMS OWL
headlines.Do-over: ROCCO BACK FOR AN ENCORE; BRINGS DRUMSTICKS

subheads.S: A textbook notch at 4k and a perfect call. The Decibelles buy musicians' earplugs in bulk.
subheads.A: No red flags and a real need: fit, then protect what's left.
subheads.B: The notch showed up; a few stamps wandered. Hoot recommends practice.
subheads.C: Look for the dip at 4k and the comeback at 8k.
subheads.Do-over: Noise notches hide between 3k and 6k. Rocco will be back next Friday.
